name: Q3Map2 2.5.17n (Quake III, experimental)
summary: Experimental: the Quake III compiler, in the three stages one program runs. Acquired by hand — there is no artifact worth pinning.
description:
Q3Map2 is one program with three stages, and that is the first thing that makes it different from the two EricW toolchains this build already ships. `qbsp`, `vis` and `light` are three executables; `-bsp`, `-vis` and `-light` are three switches on the same one, so this document declares a single executable and three actions that select a stage.

Everything below was measured by running Q3Map2 2.5.17n-git-68ecbed on Linux against a synthetic Quake III map. Nine things differ from the qualified Quake 1 line and from the experimental Quake II one, and each would have been a plausible-looking wrong answer:

1. **There is no output argument.** `q3map2 -bsp maps/x.map` writes `maps/x.bsp`, `maps/x.prt` and `maps/x.srf` BESIDE THE INPUT. So there is no `basename` option here — the compiled map is named after the map source, which is also what `+map <name>` in an engine expects — and every output is declared as a file sitting beside a staged input rather than as a path in the working directory.
2. **`-vis` and `-light` take the `.bsp` directly.** They were measured accepting it and finding the companion files of the same stem beside it.
3. **`-light` refuses to run without `<stem>.srf` AND `<stem>.map` beside the BSP.** Either one missing is `Script file … was not found` and exit 1. `-vis` needs neither: it wants the `.bsp` and the `.prt` and nothing else. That asymmetry is why the two actions declare different staged sidecars.
4. **`-vis` without `-saveprt` DELETES the portal file it was given.** This document always sends `-saveprt`, because an action handed a file must not be able to destroy it.
5. **A leak exits 0.** With `-leaktest`, a leaked map prints `--- MAP LEAKED, ABORTING LEAKTEST ---`, writes `<stem>.lin` and writes no BSP — and the process still exits 0. The compile is therefore not saved by its exit status but by its declared outputs: `bsp` is required, so the job fails because the file is not there.
6. **A missing texture or shader is a warning and exit 0** — `WARNING: Couldn't find image for shader …` — and the BSP is written anyway. With no game data bound at all the compile still succeeds and writes a BSP in which every surface has default surfaceparms. That is the Quake III counterpart of Quake II's `.wal` flags, and it is why the base game data root is required rather than optional.
7. **A face's shader name in a `.map` carries no `textures/` prefix**; Q3Map2 adds it. A map written with `textures/aucom/wall` produces `Couldn't find image for shader textures/textures/aucom/wall`, which reads like a missing file and is a doubled prefix.
8. **`-light` is nondeterministic above one thread.** Two eight-thread runs of one map produced two different BSPs; two one-thread runs produced the same one twice. The BSP stage is deterministic at any thread count.
9. **Q3Map2 always initialises a home VFS** — `~/.q3a/baseq3/` on Linux — before anything it was told about. `-fs_homepath` redirects it, and this document sends the job workspace, so a build reads what was bound to it and not whatever is in the user's home directory.

Three roots, bound separately. `tool_root` holds the executable. `game_root` and `content_root` are both passed as `-fs_basepath`, which upstream documents as repeatable and which was measured resolving a shader out of the first and its image out of the second: each is a directory that CONTAINS `baseq3/`, not a `baseq3/` itself. Q3Map2 takes a path for a basepath and a NAME for a game directory, so a mod is the `mod` option and becomes `-fs_game`, never a path. A map that uses only base game content binds `content_root` to the same directory as `game_root`.

The version probe reads the identity banner rather than the first line. Q3Map2 prints its bare version first — `2.5.17n-git-68ecbed`, with nothing around it — and a probe that took that line could not tell Q3Map2's output from any other program's.

Its own source files carry the GtkRadiant header — 'either version 2 of the License, or (at your option) any later version' — so GPL-2.0-or-later is what it is conveyed under. The surrounding NetRadiant-custom tree carries three licences at once (BSD, LGPL-2.1 and GPL, each file saying which), which is why GitHub's own detector reports the repository as `Other`; the corresponding source for the build measured here is the `20260114` tag named above. Auto-Pigeon Companion is MIT and separate: it runs this program as a separate process and does not contain, link or relicense it — and, unlike the two EricW toolchains, it does not download it either.

platforms.note: the three stages were run here on a synthetic Quake III map: compile, visibility, lighting. A claim about this program on this platform, not that Quake III is finished.

acquisition.title: Use a copy you already have
acquisition.hint: choose the directory that holds `q3map2` — inside an extracted NetRadiant-custom, that is `usr/bin`
acquisition.note: This is the route, and there is deliberately no managed download beside it. Upstream's Linux release for `20260114` is a `.7z` holding one file — an AppImage of the whole NetRadiant editor — and this program unpacks zip and tar.gz only; the Windows release is a 43 MB zip of the same editor; macOS has no artifact at all. `AUP/AUCOM 216` says not to install a map editor merely because the release bundles one, and there is no smaller artifact to prefer: `q3map2` resolves libassimp, libdraco, libminizip, libpugixml, libicu, libxml2 and libglib out of the bundle's own `../lib`, so it cannot be lifted out on its own. Keep that `lib` directory beside the `bin` you point at. On Linux, `./NetRadiant-Custom-x86_64.AppImage --appimage-extract` unpacks the bundle without installing anything.

acquisition.title: Find it on PATH
acquisition.note: Several distributions package NetRadiant, which puts `q3map2` on PATH. Whatever version is first there is what runs — the version probe below reports which, and an older 2.5.x may not behave as this document describes.

capabilities.title: Compile a Quake III map into a BSP
capabilities.description: Reads .map source and writes the Quake III BSP, the portal file the vis stage needs, and the surface file the light stage refuses to run without. A leaked map produces a .lin line file instead of a BSP.

capabilities.title: Compute the potentially visible set
capabilities.description: Rewrites the BSP with its visibility data. Quake III has no hearability pass — that is Quake II's.

capabilities.title: Compute lighting
capabilities.description: Writes the lightmaps into the BSP. It needs the surface file and the map source beside it, both measured, and it writes no separate lighting file.

actions.title: Compile the map
actions.description:
The BSP stage. `-meta` is on by default because upstream's own help says `ALWAYS USE THIS`: without it adjacent triangles of one texture are never combined and the map is slower everywhere.

The BSP, the portal file and the surface file all appear beside the staged map source, which is why none of them declares a path.

options.name: meta
options.title: Combine adjacent surfaces
options.description: Upstream's help says of `-meta`: ALWAYS USE THIS. Turn it off only to reproduce an old build.

options.name: leaktest
options.title: Stop if the map leaks
options.description: Q3Map2 writes the `.lin` line file either way and, with this on, writes no BSP. It still exits 0 — the missing BSP is what fails the job, and the `.lin` is what you load in the editor to find the hole.

options.name: mod
options.title: Mod directory name
options.description: A NAME, not a path: `-fs_game missionpack` looks for `missionpack` inside each basepath. Leave it empty for a plain base game map.

options.name: threads
options.title: Threads
options.description: The BSP stage was measured to produce the same file at any thread count. The lighting stage was not; see its own option.

options.name: patchmeta
options.title: Turn patches into triangle meshes
options.description: Patches are curved surfaces, and Auto-Pigeon's own patch support is unfinished. This is Q3Map2's own switch, and what it does to a map with patches in it has not been measured here.

options.name: custinfoparms
options.title: Read scripts/custinfoparms.txt
options.description: Loads custom surface and content flags a mod defines. Off unless your content root has that file.

options.name: samplesize
options.title: Lightmap resolution
options.description: In units per luxel — smaller is finer and slower. Leave unset for Q3Map2's own default.

roots.purpose: read the staged map source, write the BSP beside it, and hold the home directory Q3Map2 would otherwise take from the user
read the base game's shader scripts and textures, whose surfaceparms are baked into the BSP
read your own shaders and textures, which overlay the base game's

actions.title: Compute visibility
actions.description:
The VIS stage rewrites the BSP it is given, and opens the `.prt` of the same stem beside it without being told to — which is why the portal file is an input here and is staged with the BSP.

`-saveprt` is not an option. Measured: without it Q3Map2 deletes the portal file when it finishes, and an action must not be able to destroy a file it was handed.

options.name: fast
options.title: Fast, crude visibility
options.description: Upstream calls it very fast and crude. It is for looking at what you just built, not for what you ship.

options.name: mergeportals
options.title: Merge portals
options.description: Upstream: sometimes much faster, and usually does not hurt the frame rate.

options.name: mod
options.title: Mod directory name
options.description: As for the compile stage: a name, not a path.

diagnostics.message: Q3Map2 could not open a file it needs — for this stage that is normally the portal file of the same name as the BSP.
diagnostics.hint: The compile stage produces it. A leaked map has none, because the compile stops before writing one.

diagnostics.message: The BSP has no portals, so there is nothing to compute.
diagnostics.hint: A map that is one open room has one cluster and no portals. That is not an error; it means visibility has nothing to cull.

diagnostics.message: Q3Map2 stopped with an error; its next line says which.

roots.purpose: rewrite the staged BSP with its visibility data
read the base game content Q3Map2 loads at startup
read your own content, which overlays the base game's

actions.title: Compute lighting
actions.description:
The LIGHT stage writes the lightmaps into the BSP. There is no separate lighting file: Quake III lightmaps live inside the BSP, or — for a build that asked for external ones, which this document does not — in a directory beside it.

It needs two companion files beside the BSP and refuses without either: `<stem>.srf`, which the compile stage wrote, and `<stem>.map`, the map source itself. Both are staged with the BSP. A lighting job that staged only the BSP would exit 1 saying a script file was not found, and the file it named would be one nobody thought they had asked for.

options.name: fast
options.title: Fast lighting
options.description: Ignores tiny light contributions. Quick, and visibly rougher.

options.name: filter
options.title: Filter the lightmaps
options.description: Blurs the lightmap slightly, which hides sampling noise.

options.name: samples
options.title: Adaptive supersampling
options.description: Q3Map2's own `-samples`: how hard it works on the edges of shadows.

options.name: bounce
options.title: Radiosity bounces
options.description: How many times light bounces off surfaces. Each bounce costs another full pass.

options.name: shade
options.title: Phong shading
options.description: Smooths lighting across surfaces that meet at a shallow angle.

options.name: patchshadows
options.title: Shadows from patches
options.description: Patches do not cast shadows unless this is on. Auto-Pigeon's own patch support is unfinished, so a map from this editor is unlikely to have any yet.

options.name: mod
options.title: Mod directory name
options.description: As for the compile stage: a name, not a path.

options.name: threads
options.title: Threads
options.description: Measured: this stage produces a different BSP on different runs above one thread, and the same one every time at one thread. Use one when you need to compare a build with the last one byte for byte.

diagnostics.hint: Both are staged with the BSP by this profile. Seeing this means one of them was not produced by the compile stage.
